name: Battery
label: Revelation
lede: Battery started as Fury in Washington in 1990, sold better in Europe than at home, and broke up six months after its Revelation album. Twenty years on, a new song looked back at singer Brian McTernan's teenage stay in a mental hospital.

eras.title: Fury, then a long stall
eras.text: Battery started in Washington in 1990 as Fury, a youth crew band in the city that invented straight edge. It nearly ended right away, then a German label found the old songs and gave it a second life.

years.cap: Battery at the Safari Club, Washington, D.C., 1990
years.h: Five D.C. kids start a youth crew band called Fury
years.p: [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] sings, [[Ken Olden|94959ed9-83ae-46e1-b23f-88939fad93e6]] and Matt Squire play guitar, Toshi Yano plays bass and Zac Eller drums. By the first show the name is Battery.

years.h: Battery stalls when McTernan lands in a mental hospital
years.p: Depression and fights come first, by the RevHQ account. Olden and Eller go off to start Worlds Collide; McTernan starts Ashes.
years.xp: The RevHQ interview puts Battery's start in 1990, when McTernan was in eighth grade, and says the hospital stay came soon after the first show. The song My Last Breath goes back to it 27 years later.

years.h: The first 7" comes out on Deadlock Records
years.p: Everyone from the first show is on it: McTernan, Olden, Squire, Yano and Eller.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Deadlock 7" as the band's first recording, under the Battery name, in 1991.

years.h: A German label re-releases the old songs, and they sell
years.p: Lost & Found Records puts out re-recorded versions of the 7" songs as We Won't Fall. Sales are good enough that Battery re-form to record and tour Europe.
years.xp: McTernan says in the RevHQ interview that he found out in 1993 that Lost & Found had released the original Battery material and that it was selling really well.

eras.title: Better known in Europe
eras.text: At home Battery were a D.C.-area band. Lost & Found pressed the records in Europe, where the band drew, and those tours gave McTernan the confidence he later took into the studio.

years.h: Two labels split Only the Diehard Remain by continent
years.p: Tidal handles the US and Lost & Found Europe. Revelation's description: sing-along youth crew hardcore with very sincere lyrics.

years.h: In Europe Battery draw; at home they're a D.C. band
years.p: Wikipedia notes they were known mostly around D.C. in the US while doing well in Europe.
years.xp: Battery toured North America and Europe through the mid-'90s. McTernan credits the European tours with the confidence he later brought to producing other people's records.

years.cap: Battery at Coney Island High, New York, 1998
years.h: Frodus drummer Jason Hamacher joins for Until the End
years.p: The second album comes out on Conversion in the US and Lost & Found in Europe. [[Jason Hamacher|00a29c28-a1f0-4590-8055-6a94f407f19b]] plays in Battery while still drumming in [[Frodus|ea524f94-2e37-414d-a7e9-61ba96472f0a]].
years.xp: Wikipedia says bassist Ben Chused left in 1996 for Ten Yard Fight and Graham Land took over. A Buffalo show filmed on New Year's Eve 1996 survives in full.

years.src: Revelation Records: Better Than a Thousand
years.h: Olden and Ray Cappo cut Just One as [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]]
years.p: Olden's side project with Graham Land and [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] puts the record out on Revelation (REV 060). By the end, Revelation says, Cappo's voice is audibly wearing out.

years.src: Revelation Records: Battery, Whatever It Takes
years.h: Whatever It Takes is the one on Revelation
years.p: Twelve songs. A review quoted on Revelation's site calls it Battery's strongest and has one complaint, the production.

years.cap: Brian McTernan singing at Coney Island High, New York, July 1998
years.h: Six months after Whatever It Takes, Battery are done
years.p: McTernan moves on to [[Miltown|a833c30f-40e5-4b26-aaaa-906ed2d843fb]] and a producing career; Olden keeps playing in [[Damnation A.D.|52ae8d28-e8f6-4ac5-8653-c9ffcc0bfc0f]]
years.xp: McTernan says in the RevHQ interview that they broke up six months after the Revelation album came out. Wikipedia dates the end to shortly after the 1998 tours.

eras.title: Salad Days, in a Boston basement
eras.text: McTernan started recording bands at 18 in the basement of a shared house in Boston and named the studio Salad Days after the Minor Threat song. After Battery it became his main job.

years.p: A discography compilation on Soul Force Records gathers Battery's recordings from the Fury days through 1997.

eras.title: A song after twenty years
eras.text: A one-off for Revelation's 25th anniversary turned into festival offers, then a new song, a charity compilation and a European tour.

years.h: Revelation's 25th anniversary brings Battery back to New York
years.p: Offers follow from Damaged City Fest in D.C. and from REVfest.
years.xp: The reunion started as a one-off. McTernan says in the RevHQ interview that when Damaged City Fest asked, he thought it would be fun to do, and that writing again has been surprisingly easy and natural.

years.big: It felt great to write a Battery song after so many years
years.h: My Last Breath is Battery's first new song in 20 years
years.p: Ken Olden on the song, which faces McTernan's teenage years in a mental hospital and is dedicated to his daughter. It leads off Revelation's collection For the Rejected by the Rejected.
years.xp:
Proceeds go to the Center for Infant and Child Loss in Baltimore. WBGO says Mike "Phyte" Mowery's son Leo died during delivery in 2013, and that Paul Leavitt's son Casey was found dead in his crib on July 5, 2013. Leavitt recorded the song, and drummer Jason Hamacher told WBGO those losses shaped why Battery came back.

Battery toured Europe that fall.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, April 7, 2017
yt: Full set filmed by hate5six, April 7, 2017

years.h: Be Well starts up with members of Bane and Darkest Hour
years.p: McTernan fronts it. The Hard Times Noise ran the announcement in August 2020, with the band talking about a new LP.

eras.title: Back on Revelation, behind the desk
eras.text: McTernan's studio work kept him in the Revelation family long after Battery's last record.

years.h: Say Less puts McTernan on a Revelation record, as producer
years.p: [[Calling Hours|a76e3280-2524-461d-855f-0550ebedff93]], the band of [[Farside|c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069]] singer Popeye Vogelsang, release it November 10. McTernan produced it and helped steer it to Revelation.
